title: Protocol: Sonication-based Circular Chromosome Conformation Capture with next-generation sequencing analysis for the detection of chromatin interactions
protocol: Add 540 μl of fresh formaldehyde (37% stock) to treated MCF-7 human breast adenocarcinoma cells growing in a 150 mm diameter plate in 20 ml of media to obtain a final concentration of 1% formaldehyde for cross-linking.
Rotate the plate on a belly dancer for 10 min at 22°C.
Add 2 ml of 2.5 M filter-sterilized glycine to stop the cross-linking.
Rotate on a belly dancer for 5 min at 22°C.
Pour away the medium into a waste flask.
Wash cells twice with 10 ml of cold \(4°C) 1x PBS with gentle shaking.
Pour away the PBS into a waste flask.
Add 2 ml of 1x PBS and 2 ml of trypsin to each plate.
Mix well and let the plates sit for 10 min at 22°C.
Add 4 ml of growth media to stop the trypsinization.
Use a blade scraper to scrape off the cells.
Collect cells into a 15 ml falcon tube.
Wash the plates with 4 ml of 1x PBS and place these cells into the same 15 ml falcon tube.
Pellet cells at 3,000 rpm \(800xg, Eppendorf) for 15 min at 4°C and remove the supernatant.
Wash the pellet with 5 ml of 1x PBS, then pellet cells at 3,000 rpm \(800xg, Eppendorf) for 5 min at 4°C and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend and wash each pellet with 5 ml of Triton X-100 lysis buffer.
Incubate at 4°C with gentle agitation \(Stuart Roller Mixer SRT9\) for 30 minutes.
Spin at 3,000 rpm \(800xg, Eppendorf) for 5 min at 4°C and pour away supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet (nuclear lysate) with 600 μl SDS lysis buffer.
Sonicate the nuclear lysate for 8 min using the Bioruptor, operated in a 4°C cold room at high power: 30 seconds on, 30 seconds off.
Pellet cell debris at 13,000 rpm (15700xg) for 10 minutes at 4°C and transfer the supernatant (chromatin) into a fresh 1.7 ml tube.
Store the chromatin at -80°C.
Add 6.5 µl of 20% Triton-X to a 125 μl aliquot of sonicated, cross-linked chromatin containing 0.1% SDS.
Thaw chromatin samples gently on ice.
Allow thawed chromatin to equilibrate at 37°C for 1 hour.
Centrifuge chromatin in a microcentrifuge at maximum speed for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Remove and keep the supernatant after centrifugation.
Add 0.1% SDS to chromatin samples if not present, or dilute excess SDS with Buffer EB.
Mix well and let equilibrated chromatin stand at 37°C for 1 hour if SDS adjustments were made.
Prepare an end-blunting reaction mix by combining 263 µl of DNA from two 125 μl aliquots of chromatin, 33 µl of 10x End-Repair Buffer, 15 µl of 2.5mM dNTP Mix, and 15 µl of 10mM ATP.
Add 5 µl of End-Repair Enzyme Mix to the end-blunting reaction mix.
Incubate the end-blunting reaction mix at room temperature for 45 minutes.
Set up a ligation reaction by combining 330 μl of DNA, 5 ml of 10x T4 DNA Ligase Buffer (NEB), and 166 µl of T4 DNA Ligase (30u/µl, Fermentas).
Add 44.5 ml of water with 1x protease inhibitor to the ligation reaction mix.
Incubate the ligation reaction at 16°C overnight (at least 16 hours).
Perform reverse cross-linking by adding 375 µl of Proteinase K (20 mg/ml).
Mix by inverting the tube several times.
Incubate at 65°C overnight (at least 16 hours).
Split each ligation reaction into three 16.7 ml portions.
Transfer each portion to a separate Maxtract High Density (50 ml) tube.
Add an equal volume of phenol-chloroform to each tube and mix by inverting for about 2 min.
Centrifuge at 1800 × g (3000 rpm), 5 min, room temperature (22-25°C).
Pre-pellet the phase lock gel in the Maxtract tubes by centrifugation at 1800 × g (3000 rpm), 5 min, room temperature.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a 50-ml Nalgene PPCO tube.
Add sodium acetate (3 M, pH 5.2) and Glycoblue to the aqueous phase.
Add isopropanol to the mixture.
Incubate at -80°C for at least 1 hour.
Pre-chill the Sorvall centrifuge to 4°C.
Pellet the DNA at 38730 × g (18000 rpm), 30 min, 4°C using the SS-34 fixed rotor.
Carefully decant the supernatant and wash the pellet twice with 30 ml 75% ethanol.
Allow the pellet to air dry in a laminar flow hood.
Re-suspend the pellet in 100 µl EB buffer.
Quantitate the DNA concentration using Picogreen Fluorimetry.
Incubate DNA with RNase A at 37°C for 30 min.
Purify DNA using phenol-chloroform extraction followed by isopropanol precipitation.
Resuspend each sample in 50 μl of EB buffer and quantitate using Picogreen.
Remove non-circular DNA by incubating the reaction mixture overnight at 37°C.
Inactivate plasmid-safe DNase by incubating samples at 70°C for 20 min.
Purify DNA using phenol-chloroform extraction followed by isopropanol precipitation.
Resuspend in 100 μl of EB buffer and quantitate using Picogreen.
Set the PCR machine to run at 98 °C for 30 seconds followed by 20 cycles of 98 °C for 10 seconds, 72 °C for 30 seconds, and then hold at 4 °C after completion.
Add 1 µl of undiluted product from inverse PCR to the reaction mixture.
Add 1 µl of nested, adaptor B-tailed primer (biotinylated) (25 µM) to the reaction mixture.
Add 1 µl of nested, adaptor A-tailed primer (25 µM) to the reaction mixture.
Mix with 25 µl of 2 x Phusion Master Mix and 22 µl of nuclease-free H2O for a total volume of 50 µl.
Run PCR products on a 4-20% TBE PAGE gel at 200 V for 40 minutes in a Novex mini-cell.
Stain the gel with SYBR Green for 15 minutes in the dark and visualize under DarkReader.
Observe a smear band across approximately 200bp to >600bp range on the gel.
Carry out additional nested PCR reactions using products from the first round of inverse PCR.
Prepare at least four 50 µl reactions for each subsequent nested PCR.
Run PCR products in a 6% TBE PAGE gel for 30 min at 200V in a Novex mini-cell.
Stain the gel with SYBR Green for 15 min in the dark.
Visualize the stained gel on a DarkReader.
Excise the smear band in the region of 400bp to >600bp using a sharp scalpel and gel-handler sheets.
Take photos of the gel before and after excision.
Purify the excised DNA by the gel-crush protocol.
Resuspend the purified pellet in 40 µl TE buffer.
Quantitate DNA concentration using Picogreen.
Perform a quality control check using an Agilent DNA 7500 LabChip according to the manufacturer’s guidelines.
Prepare and sequence the sample with Roche 454 Titanium sequencing according to the manufacturer’s guidelines.
